clue.text: Make fast progress in profession

definitions.meaning: a ... is one's working life or occupation

explanation.surface: Someone getting ahead quickly at work.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to hurtle along; as a noun it is a lifelong occupation.

clue.text: Forbearance evident in a g & s work

definitions.meaning: forbearance is calm tolerance of delay or trouble
G & S is Gilbert and Sullivan, whose comic operas include one of this name

explanation.surface: A quality of restraint is shown in a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan were a Victorian British writing team of comic operas; 'Patience' (1881) is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Forbearance is a synonym for calm tolerance, and the second sense names the 1881 comic opera.

clue.text: What a roundsman must do to perform adequately

definitions.meaning: a roundsman is a British delivery man, such as a milkman, who must bring orders to the door
an idiom for doing what is expected or promised

explanation.surface: A delivery man's duty is also what anyone must do to do the job properly.
explanation.walkthrough: A roundsman is a British tradesman who makes regular delivery rounds, like a milkman.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the delivery man's task of bringing merchandise; idiomatically, meeting expectations.

clue.text: Succeed in act to disconnect?

definitions.meaning: to manage a difficult feat successfully
literally to tug something away so it detaches

explanation.surface: A question about whether separating something counts as a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically it means achieving a tricky feat; literally it means tugging something away so it comes apart.

clue.text: Rooks flying? Such may be a figment of the imagination

definitions.meaning: in chess a rook is also called a castle, so rooks aloft would be castles up high

explanation.surface: Birds in flight are offered as an example of something imagined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rooks' suggests birds, which suits 'flying', but the chess piece is meant: a rook is also called a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes impractical daydreams, and whimsically pictures chess pieces airborne.

clue.text: Mother gains employment in heritage centre

indicators.note: Mother gains something by taking it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother
use means employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: A mother finds a job at a heritage site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gains' is a container signal here: the mother takes the job inside herself rather than earning wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A heritage centre is a place exhibiting historical objects, much like a gallery of artefacts.

clue.text: Gala money initiator of tombola brought in

indicators.note: the letter is brought inside the word for money

parts.note: a fee is money paid for a service

indicators.note: the initiator of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gala raises money and starts with a tombola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initiator of' gives T from tombola, and 'brought in' places it inside FEE. A tombola is a British raffle with prizes drawn from a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive public event, as is a summer fair held outdoors.

clue.text: Slightly crazy joke, beginning of act

parts.note: a gag is a joke

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mildly mad joke opens a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for mentally confused or dotty.

clue.text: English copper coin once used in France

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An English copper coin that used to circulate in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper coin' reads as one thing, but copper is the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: The écu was an old French silver or gold piece, later also a European currency unit.

clue.text: Charm may be shown by a stubborn creature with time

parts.note: a mule is famously obstinate

explanation.surface: A good-luck token might be displayed by an obstinate animal over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm worn to ward off evil is a protective talisman.

clue.text: A particularly beautiful thing in one constellation

parts.note: a gem is something especially lovely or prized
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something especially beautiful found in a single star group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins is a zodiac star group, named in Latin.

clue.text: Machine very hot and covered in foam

parts.note: a lathe is a machine that turns material for shaping
red-hot, so red means very hot

explanation.surface: A machine overheats and ends up foaming.
explanation.definitionFit: Lather is soapy froth, so something coated in it is soaped or frothy.

clue.text: Hamlet performance, kind that is out of the ordinary

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of their ordinary order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A review of an unusual staging of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the ordinary' rearranges the letters of PERFORMANCE and KIND; 'that is' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's title in Shakespeare's play is the heir of the Danish throne.

clue.text: Part of what fisherman needs to get perch

definitions.meaning: an angler's kit includes a pole with a line
a perch is an old unit of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole

explanation.surface: An angler needs the right kit to catch a perch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' suggests the fish, but it is an old British unit of length, equal to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishing pole is part of angling tackle, and an old land measure goes by the same name as a perch.

clue.text: Pardon girl outside home

indicators.note: the girl's name sits outside, wrapped round the word for home

parts.note: Amy is a girl's name
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: Forgive a young woman standing outside her house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pardon' reads as an apology opening the sentence, but it is the definition; 'outside' wraps the girl around her home.
explanation.definitionFit: An official pardon granted to many offenders at once is a general forgiveness.

clue.text: Fellow a lot cut short

indicators.note: the word is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: many means a lot

explanation.surface: A man with a large amount is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the last letter, Y, from MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow is a synonym for a chap or guy.

clue.text: Woman married country attorney in the united states

parts.note: Iran is a country
a DA is a district attorney, the American public prosecutor

explanation.surface: A woman marries a lawyer from America.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female given name, as in Shakespeare's heroine in The Tempest.

clue.text: Various metals, including silver, featured in ancient treatise

indicators.note: the shuffled letters include the symbol for silver within them
various suggests the letters are mixed into a different order

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An old scientific work discusses different metals, silver among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' scrambles the fodder before 'including' takes in the silver symbol, so the metals word never appears whole; the shuffle gives ALMEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The Almagest is Ptolemy's second-century astronomical work, a classical treatise.

clue.text: Is this shield easily knocked out of shape?

definitions.text: Is this shield easily knocked out of shape?

parts.words: Is this shield easily knocked out of shape?
parts.note: a small round shield is pictured as something that warps or bends easily, as if it were a thing that buckles

explanation.surface: A question about whether a piece of armour dents easily.
explanation.walkthrough: A metal sheet that bends under pressure buckles; the question jokes that the small round shield's name suggests it does just that.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckler is a small round shield held by a handle.

clue.text: A tenement lit-up, a shambles two from the end of the row

definitions.text: two from the end of the row

indicators.note: a shambles is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lit-up block of flats is in a mess near the end of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shambles' rearranges A, TENEMENT, LITUP and A; the second 'a' is fodder too, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The penultimate is next to last, so this one is third from last, two places before the end.

clue.text: Subsequently found in the east twice — that's a gas

indicators.note: one word is found inside the pair of letters
the abbreviation is written two times

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
then means subsequently

explanation.surface: Something later discovered in the east, twice over, turns out to be a gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' doubles E (east) to EE and 'found in' puts THEN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethene, or ethylene, is a simple hydrocarbon that is gaseous at room temperature.

clue.text: Old coin for leather-worker

explanation.surface: A craftsman working hides is linked to an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was British slang for the sixpenny piece, withdrawn after decimalisation in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the pre-decimal sixpence, and also a craftsman who cures animal hides.

clue.text: Volume of money transacted

parts.note: reads like an amount of trade, but volume means a book, here a ledger recording payments

explanation.surface: A report on the amount of trade done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a quantity of business; it means a book, the ledger recording receipts and payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledger recording receipts and payments of money is a book of transactions.

clue.text: Plant must be given a drink

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A plant must be watered, or given something stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a flowering plant, the lily family of cuckoo-pint.

clue.text: Machine no good a German admits

indicators.note: the German word admits, or lets in, the abbreviation

parts.note: eine is German for a

explanation.surface: A German confesses that a device is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' reads as confessing, but it is a container: the German article lets the abbreviation in.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a motor or mechanical device converting energy into motion.

clue.text: Game at home little boy spoilt

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
in means at home
Ed is a short form of Edward, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A little boy ruins a game played indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruined is a synonym for damaged or wrecked.

clue.text: Priest contributing to the liturgy

indicators.note: the letters contribute to, so form part of, the phrase

explanation.surface: A cleric takes part in leading the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributing to' shows the answer sits within THE LITURGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Eli was the Old Testament priest at Shiloh who raised Samuel.

clue.text: The lady died in a shack

parts.note: she refers to a lady

explanation.surface: A woman passed away in a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A shack is a rough hut, like a small garden outbuilding.
